title: Kestrel and the Alibi Again
premise: When the coffin of town founder Edmund Kestrel is exhumed for a bicentennial ceremony and found empty, coroner Lior Amberdale discovers the burial records were forged forty years ago — and that the 'dead' witness to Kestrel's true fate may still be alive. Lior's investigation collides with Detective Mara Voss, whose duty-bound pursuit of Lior for obstruction mirrors the growing love between them. The trail leads to a hidden network of townspeople who have protected Kestrel's secret — and his survival — for decades, forcing Lior to choose between exposing a justice the law can no longer serve and preserving a fragile belonging. In the end, Lior finds the witness, Kestrel himself, dying and ready to confess, and must decide whether the truth belongs to the law, the town, or the grave.
about_author: August Blackwood is the pen name of a former rural registrar who spent a decade cataloguing the quiet secrets of small-town death records. They write mysteries about the people history buries twice.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Establishing Lior's intimate knowledge of the town's dead as they prepare founder Edmund Kestrel's coffin for ceremonial exhumation. A quiet unease settles when Lior notices the 1984 burial permit bears a signature that doesn't match the registrar's hand. Emotional beat: belonging to a town through its graves.

chapters.title: Empty Oak
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Before two hundred witnesses, the coffin is opened and found empty except for a brass key and a child's shoe. The crowd's shock curdles into suspicion of Lior, who certified the original burial. Detective Mara Voss arrives from the county and immediately distrusts them. Emotional beat: public humiliation and the first spark of antagonism.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Revisited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara reviews Lior's history: three deaths ruled accidents that Lior quietly reclassified. She suspects a pattern of vigilante interference. Meanwhile Lior privately matches the brass key to the old registrar's office. Emotional beat: the reader sees both investigators are right and wrong about each other.

chapters.title: The Forged Hand
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the archive cellar, Lior confirms the 1984 signature was forged by the beloved late registrar, Ruth Calloway — Lior's own mentor. A note in Ruth's ledger reads: 'He is not where we say. Ask the one who weeps at the wrong grave.' Emotional beat: betrayal braided with grief.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following Ruth's clue, Lior stakes out the grave of a woman whose family has visited obsessively for forty years — and catches elderly Tom Wicker leaving fresh flowers on a stranger's stone. Tom flees, dropping a photograph of a living Edmund Kestrel taken a decade ago. Emotional beat: the dead witness breathes.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara questions Lior formally; the interview becomes an unexpected exchange of confidences over shared whiskey. Lior reveals nothing of the photograph but admits the three 'accidents' were murders they couldn't prove. Mara, unsettled, recognizes a fellow truth-seeker. Emotional beat: grudging respect kindling attraction.

chapters.title: What the Wicker Knew
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior confronts Tom Wicker at his farm, where the old man confesses: in 1984 he witnessed Kestrel's murder of a business partner — but Kestrel didn't die; the town's founding families faked his death and hid him as punishment and protection. Then Tom is found dead the next morning, staged as a fall. Emotional beat: dread — the secret kills its keepers.

chapters.title: Accident Number Four
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara investigates Tom's death and finds Lior's fingerprints on the farm gate. Evidence mounts against Lior, who cannot explain their presence without exposing the investigation. Mara arrests them, hating how easily it comes. Emotional beat: duty tightening like a noose around love.

chapters.title: Held Without a Grave
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In custody, Lior reconstructs the 1984 conspiracy from memory and Ruth's ledger, realizing the founding families' descendants still hold power — including the current mayor. Mara visits off the record; Lior gives her the brass key and a plea: open Ruth's safe-deposit box. Emotional beat: trust as an act of faith.

chapters.title: Ruth's Deposit
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The box contains Kestrel's confession letter, a second key, and Ruth's coded list of the six families who hid him. Mara must choose: turn it over to a DA entangled with the mayor, or work outside the law with the suspect she's falling for. Emotional beat: justice versus procedure.

chapters.title: The Six Families
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, released on technicality. Lior and Mara, now uneasy allies, trace the descendants. Five are elderly and frightened; one, councilman Alden Pryce, is newly rich and nervous. Someone ransacks Lior's office that night — the ledger is gone. Emotional beat: the conspiracy is awake and closing in.

chapters.title: Ash on the Ledger
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The burned remains of Ruth's ledger surface in the river; a county archivist who helped them is hospitalized in a suspicious crash. Mara realizes the conspiracy reaches beyond Halloway into county institutions. She and Lior go fully off-book. Emotional beat: no safe ground left; only each other.

chapters.title: Where Weeping Ends
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Re-reading Ruth's phrase 'ask the one who weeps,' Lior realizes the wrong grave belongs to Kestrel's daughter, who died believing her father abandoned her. Her surviving son, Daniel, has tended it for years. Daniel, confronted, admits he visits his grandfather — Edmund Kestrel, alive at ninety-one, in the old sanatorium. Emotional beat: the witness everyone swears is dead.

chapters.title: The Sanatorium Wing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara and Lior reach the shuttered wing where Kestrel has lived under a false name for forty years. They find signs of a recent visitor — Alden Pryce — and Kestrel's room freshly emptied. A nurse is found sedated. Someone got there first. Emotional beat: hope snatched at the threshold.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Confession
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Daniel reveals Kestrel left a full recorded confession with him, to be released only on his death — the true account of the 1984 killing, self-defense covered up by the founding families who then imprisoned him in silence. Alden Pryce has been hunting the recording for years. Emotional beat: the truth exists, but owning it is lethal.

chapters.title: Hunt on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Pryce's men intercept Daniel; Mara and Lior flee with him through the winter woods above town, a chase that strips away all pretense of procedure. Mara takes a bullet in the shoulder shielding Lior. Emotional beat: love confessed in adrenaline and blood.

chapters.title: The Bicentennial Stage
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Pryce announces he has 'found Kestrel's remains' and plans a state funeral to bury the truth forever. Lior realizes the ceremony — the whole town watching — is the only stage big enough for a confession Pryce can't suppress. They have two days. Emotional beat: turning the town itself into the weapon.

chapters.title: What the Living Bury
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara gambles her career, delivering Kestrel's recording to the one incorruptible judge — and to the five frightened family descendants, offering them amnesty for testimony against Pryce. Four accept. Pryce, tipped off, moves to seize Daniel and the original recording. Emotional beat: duty finally aligned with conscience.

chapters.title: Edmund Kestrel, Living
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the funeral, as the casket is lowered, Lior stops the ceremony and plays the recording: Kestrel's voice confessing the 1984 killing, the cover-up, and naming Pryce's father as his jailer. The town erupts. Pryce, exposed, attempts to flee with Daniel as hostage. Emotional beat: the dead witness testifies at last.

chapters.title: The Grave That Waited
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The climax: a standoff at the empty Kestrel grave itself, where Pryce is cornered by the descendants he threatened, the judge's warrant, and Mara's drawn weapon. Daniel is freed; Pryce surrenders to the town he betrayed rather than the law that failed it. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, witnessed by everyone.

chapters.title: Ninety-One Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior visits the dying Edmund Kestrel in protective custody. He asks not for forgiveness but to be buried at last in the coffin that waited forty years. Lior, keeper of graves, grants him a real burial — and lets the town mourn a man it never knew. Emotional beat: mercy beyond judgment.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Months later: Lior reinstated, Mara transferred to Halloway by choice, the two of them tending Ruth Calloway's repaired headstone together. Lior adds a new name to their mental ledger of graves — and decides some names are better kept among the living. Emotional beat: belonging, love, and quiet justice settled like fresh earth.
